content:
You draft referral notes that a primary care provider (PCP) sends to a specialist. The PCP will review, edit and sign your draft, so write it in the PCP's voice, ready to send.

The reader is a specialist who has never met this patient and is triaging many referrals. They need to know quickly why the patient is being sent now, what question the PCP wants answered, what has already been tried or worked up, and anything that would change how they manage the patient. Lead with that. Leave out chart content this specialist has no use for.

Your source is a structured chart extract plus whatever the PCP typed, including their answers to follow-up questions. Every clinical statement in the note must come from one of those. The extract has no free-text notes, so symptoms, examination findings, functional status and patient preferences are absent unless the PCP supplied them; do not supply them yourself. When something this specialist would expect is missing, a follow-up question was left unanswered, or two entries in the chart disagree, say so in the final section so the PCP can fill it in before sending. A note that reads complete but contains an invented detail is worse than one with a visible gap.

Give dates for results and events. For a trend, state the direction with the first and latest values and their dates rather than listing every reading.

Format: plain text with no markdown, because the draft goes into an editable text field. Put each section heading in capitals on its own line, in this order:

REASON FOR REFERRAL
CLINICAL QUESTION
RELEVANT HISTORY
CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
KEY RESULTS
WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING

If the PCP gave no clinical question, propose the one the data best supports and mark it "[suggested - confirm]". Aim for one page, roughly 250 to 400 words. Start directly with the first heading; do not add a greeting, sign-off or commentary about the draft.

<referral_request>
Referring to: Cardiology
Referral condition: Ischemic heart disease / chronic heart failure
Urgency: urgent
PCP's clinical question: (none given)
PCP's additional notes: Reason for referral now: worsening breathlessness over two weeks, now breathless after walking across a room, with new swelling of both ankles. She is sleeping on three pillows.
</referral_request>

<what_this_specialist_needs>
The cardiologist will want: the cardiac diagnoses with dates, prior events and interventions (MI, PCI, CABG, heart failure admissions), latest ejection fraction and cardiac imaging, current cardiac medications (antiplatelet, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, diuretic) and obvious gaps in them, blood pressure and heart rate, lipid and glycemic control, renal function and potassium, recent emergency or inpatient encounters, and smoking status.
</what_this_specialist_needs>

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Urgent referral of Kam Harris, an 85-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease (CABG 2009-08-30) and chronic heart failure (LVEF 39.2% on 2025-05-26). Over the past two weeks her breathlessness has worsened, and she is now breathless after walking across a room. She has new bilateral ankle swelling and is sleeping on three pillows. Recent blood pressure has been persistently low (85/46 on 2026-11-16). She was admitted to hospice for heart failure on 2026-07-06.

CLINICAL QUESTION
[suggested - confirm] Please assess for acute decompensated heart failure and advise on management, including whether she needs admission. Please also advise how to optimize her heart failure regimen given her low blood pressure, declining renal function and hospice status.

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease from 2009-08-17. Abnormal cardiac imaging 2009-08-25. CABG 2009-08-30. No MI or PCI recorded.
- Chronic heart failure diagnosed 2025-04-27.
- ED visit and ICU admission for heart failure on 2025-11-22. She received IV furosemide from 2025-11-22 to 2025-12-06 and heart failure education on 2025-12-07.
- Urgent care visits on 2026-03-16, 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-12. Reasons are not recorded.
- Hospice admission 2026-07-06. Telemedicine heart failure follow-up since then, most recently 2026-11-16.
- Never smoked.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (since 2009)
- Simvastatin 20 mg (since 2009)
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg (since 2009)
- Carvedilol 25 mg (started 2026-11-09)
- Losartan 50 mg (started 2026-11-09)
- Furosemide 40 mg oral (started 2026-11-09)
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray as needed
- Metformin ER 500 mg and alendronate 10 mg
- No MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor recorded.
- No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- BP: systolic fell from 108 (2017-11-27) to 79 to 92 since 2026-09-21. Latest 85/46 (2026-11-16).
- HR: 61 (2026-11-09).
- NT-proBNP: 1963.1 (2025-04-27), 1584.4 (2025-12-06). None since.
- hs-troponin I: 0 on all 16 readings, 2025-04-27 to 2025-12-06.
- eGFR: fell from 100.6 (2017-11-27) to 36.2 (2026-11-09). Fluctuating, with 62.5 on 2026-10-19.
- Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL (2026-11-09).
- K: 4.5 mmol/L. Na: 141.3 mmol/L (2026-11-09).
- LDL: rose from 56 (2017-11-27) to 96.3 (2026-11-09). Peak 144.8 on 2026-06-29.
- HbA1c: 5.4% (2026-11-09).
- Hb: 12.2 g/dL (2025-12-06). None since.
- Weight: 77.6 kg (2026-11-09).

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
- Stress test and NYHA assessment on 2025-04-27. Results and class are not in the extract.
- Echocardiogram 2025-05-26 showed EF 39.2%. No repeat since.
- ECGs on 2025-04-27 and 2025-11-22.
- Chest radiograph 2025-11-22.
- Report text is not available for any of these.
- Heart failure self-management plan in place.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS

- Anemia.
- Hypertriglyceridemia.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Hospice status and goals of care: is she still enrolled, and what are her and her family's wishes about admission, escalation and resuscitation?
- Both metoprolol succinate and carvedilol are listed as active. Please confirm which beta blocker she is actually taking.
- Losartan, carvedilol and furosemide were all started 2026-11-09 despite systolic BP in the 80s. Please confirm the doses and how she has tolerated them.
- Please add current vitals, weight trend, oxygen saturation and examination findings. Recorded weight has been unchanged at 77.6 kg since 2026-03.
- The problem list says CKD stage 2, but eGFR 36 fits stage 3b. Please also confirm whether metformin is appropriate.
- Oxygen saturation was recorded as 79% throughout the 2025-12 admission. Is this accurate?
- Why was no MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor used?
- What were the reasons for the 2026 urgent care visits?
- Do you want an NT-proBNP and hemoglobin drawn now?
